The failing test `test_changeDefault_Locale_DateTimeInstance` is testing the `FastDateFormat` class in the `org.apache.commons.lang.time` package. The test changes the default locale, retrieves instances of date-time format using different styles and locales, and then asserts that the locales of the formats match the expected values and that the instances are not the same.

The current bug report indicates that the `FastDateFormat getDateInstance()` and `getDateTimeInstance()` methods assume that `Locale.getDefault()` won't change. If the default locale is changed after creating instances without specifying a locale, the wrong locale may be applied.

From the code snippets of the `FastDateFormat` class:
1. The `getDateInstance(int style, Locale locale)` method is used to retrieve a date-only format instance with the specified style and locale.
2. The `getDateTimeInstance(int dateStyle, int timeStyle, Locale locale)` method is used to retrieve a date-time format instance with the specified date and time styles and locale.

Based on the information provided and the bug report, it seems that changing the default locale after creating date or date-time format instances without specifying a locale could result in unexpected behavior because the instances are created using the current default locale at that time.

To address the issue described in the bug report, it may be necessary to ensure that date and date-time format instances are created with the correct locale even if the default locale changes. One possible solution could involve modifying the `FastDateFormat` class to consider the locale explicitly when creating format instances, regardless of the default locale.

Next, I will suggest specific methods in the `FastDateFormat` class that could be fixed to address this issue.
```java
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int, java.util.Locale)
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(int, int, java.util.Locale)
```

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
